The DID.is public API answers questions about decentralized identifiers, credentials and AI agents over plain HTTPS and JSON. It is anonymous and free, and it has 20 operations, described in a machine-readable [OpenAPI document](https://did.is/api/openapi.json) and on the [API reference](/reference/api/) page.

Every answer **reports evidence and states its limits**. The API does not give trust scores and does not decide for you. Your application applies its own rules to the result.

## What you get

- **Anonymous access.** No API key and no account are needed.
- **JSON results** with a plain-language headline and the checks behind it.
- **Stable error codes** in RFC 9457 problem objects.

## What it does not give you

- **Private lookups.** Public resolutions may appear in the identifier's public observation history (not linked to who asked). For identifiers you must not disclose, use private resolution in the [console](/app/accounts/).
- **Unlimited volume.** Each client has a request budget (see below). For higher volume, use a project API key from the [console](/app/accounts/).

## Base URL

```text
https://did.is/api
```

All requests use HTTPS.

<Tabs syncKey="lang">
<TabItem label="curl">
```bash
curl https://did.is/api/v1/resolve/did:key:z6MkhaXgBZDvotDkL5257faiztiGiC2QtKLGpbnnEGta2doK
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="TypeScript">
```ts
import { DidisClient } from "@didis/client";

const didis = new DidisClient(); // https://did.is/api
const r = await didis.resolve("did:key:z6MkhaXgBZDvotDkL5257faiztiGiC2QtKLGpbnnEGta2doK");
console.log(r.verdict.headline);
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">
```python
from didis import DidisClient

with DidisClient() as didis:  # https://did.is/api
    r = didis.resolve("did:key:z6MkhaXgBZDvotDkL5257faiztiGiC2QtKLGpbnnEGta2doK")
    print(r["verdict"]["headline"])
```
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Request budgets

Each client has two budgets:

| Budget | Limit | Endpoints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | 20 requests per minute | Resolution, dereferencing, history, diff, graph, fast verify, claims, directory, `verify-tool`, status |
| Intensive | 10 requests per minute | `/v1/stream`, `/v1/credentials/verify`, `/v1/policies/evaluate`, `/v1/mcp/inspect`, `/v1/a2a/inspect`, `/v1/agents/verify-delegation`, `/v1/agents/authorize` |

Resolving a `did:webvh` identifier also uses the intensive budget. `/health` is not budgeted.

When a budget is used up, the API answers `429` with a `Retry-After` header. See [Errors and rate limits](/build/errors/).

## Encoding identifiers

Put the DID in the path as is. Percent-encoding is also accepted; the API decodes the path exactly once.

- `#` must be encoded as `%23`, otherwise HTTP clients drop the fragment: `/v1/dereference/did:web:did.is%23key-1`.
- The SDKs encode identifiers for you.

## Reading the response

| You receive | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` with `application/json` | A result. It can still say `INVALID`, `FAIL` or `DENY`. | Read the status fields of that endpoint. |
| `application/did` or `application/did-resolution` | The W3C endpoint `/1.0/identifiers/{did}`. | Read it as a W3C DID resolution result. |
| `text/event-stream` | The live stream `/v1/stream/{did}`. | See [Live stream](/build/stream/). |
| `application/problem+json` | No result could be produced. | Use the `code`. See [Errors and rate limits](/build/errors/). |
| `429` or `503` with `Retry-After` | Budget used up, or service busy. | Wait that many seconds. |

Other conventions:

- Responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Request bodies are limited to 512 KiB.
- A request that takes longer than 45 seconds is ended with `408`.

## Service status

- `GET /health` reports the supported methods and standards.
- `GET /v1/status` reports the status of each component. The same information is on [did.is/status](https://did.is/status).

```bash
curl https://did.is/api/v1/status
```
